body:
## Problem

Reported by the user: the web app logs them out "after more than half a day or so"
of not visiting the site, while the Android app never does.

Root cause is NOT a timeout — nothing expired at all:

- The web client stored the bearer token and account in `sessionStorage`
  (`web/src/api/client.ts`, `web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx`). `sessionStorage` is
  scoped to the browsing session, so it dies when the tab closes — and on mobile,
  whenever the browser reclaims a backgrounded tab. That reclaim is what the user
  was hitting roughly daily.
- Server-side, `auth_tokens` had no expiry column and `require_account()` never
  checked age, so a token lived forever until an explicit logout/revoke. Combined
  with the above, every reclaimed web tab minted a *new* session row that nothing
  ever cleaned up, so Settings → Sessions stacked up phantom "web" entries.

## Fix

1. Web token + account move to `localStorage`, so a session survives a tab
   reclaim / browser restart.
2. Real server-side sliding **inactivity** expiry, per session, so persisting the
   token durably doesn't mean forever:
   - web: 7 days idle
   - android: 62 days idle
   New `auth_tokens.idle_ttl_ms` column (migration 3). The window is resolved
   server-side from a `platform` hint the client sends at login
   (`auth.resolve_idle_ttl_ms`) — a client picks a bucket, never a duration.
   Unknown/absent platform falls back to the long default so a pre-T-104 client
   is never logged out early.
3. Expiry is enforced in `require_account()` (401 `session_expired`, row deleted
   on sight) *and* swept by `gc.run()`, so an abandoned session can't linger
   forever in the table.
4. Sessions list hides idle-expired rows, and both clients now show a "last
   activity" line per session (the `last_seen_at` was already on the wire,
   just never rendered).

Session stacking is fixed from both ends: localStorage stops minting a new row
per tab reclaim, and the 7-day sweep clears the existing backlog.

## Notes / trade-offs

- A stolen token can still be kept alive indefinitely by polling; idle expiry is
  a "forgotten/abandoned device" control, not an anti-attacker one.
- The `platform` hint is self-asserted. That's acceptable for the same reason:
  the client already holds the token and can refresh it at will.
- First real exercise of the T-57 migration machinery. Verified end-to-end
  against a database built from the actual v1.5.0 schema: auto-migrates on
  connect, stamps user_version 3, backfills `device_label = 'web'` rows to 7 days
  and everything else to 62.
title: Web sessions die with the browser tab; no server-side session expiry at all
